newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PAL employees stage walkout at Manila airport.
newsitem.headline: PAL employees stage walkout at Manila airport.

text.p: Scores of employees of the Philippine Airlines (PAL) walked off their jobs at the Manila international airport on Wednesday evening in what their leaders said was the beginning of a strike.

The estimated 150 workers, comprising the airline's rank and file, staged the walkout after President Fidel Ramos rejected a plea by PAL workers to intervene in their long-running pay dispute with the national carrier, saying he wasn't a labour arbiter.
"There are indications that they are on a strike," a source at PAL management told Reuters.

It was not immediately clear if all of PALEA's nearly 9,000 members had joined the walkout and what the effect of the walkout had been so far on operations of PAL and other airlines at Manila's domestic and international airports.
PAL ground crew provides catering and cargo services to a number of foreign airlines flying to and out of Manila.

Three PAL unions, including PALEA and unions representing the pilots and cabin crew, on Tuesday urged Ramos to intervene to help avert a potentially embarrassing strike while the government is preparing for next month's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum summit which Ramos is hosting.
"I passed (the union request) immediately to the (labour department) because I should not be a labour arbiter," Ramos told a news conference.
